source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: The projected Brownian integrand with measurable temperature. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: The definition constructs the strongly progressive product-space $L^2$ integrand for noise entry $(i,j)$ with the representative shown below.
assumptions: The filtration is indexed by nonnegative real time. The sample measure is finite, and the coordinate set $I$ is finite with decidable equality.
The process $X$ takes values in the Euclidean unit sphere, is jointly measurable for the product of the time Borel and sample measurable structures, and is strongly progressive.

For the selected horizon $T\ge0$, the real deterministic temperature is Borel measurable on nonnegative time and bounded in absolute value pointwise on $[0,T]$. The square root is the total real square root.
The symbol $\ell_T$ denotes Lebesgue time restricted to $[0,T]$. The $L^2$ membership uses $\mu\otimes\ell_T$, in sample-first order.
source_evidence.boundary: The representative is defined at all nonnegative times. The $L^2$ assertion uses the selected horizon.
